jobs.text:
Hyperliquid made $19.2 million in a week, and I do not read it as growth.

Open interest fell 17.2% over the same days, and I read that as fees from traders closing out, not joining in.

Show me open interest recovering and I will call it growth.

$HYPE #Hyperliquid

$24.86 billion of Bitcoin sits in government wallets. One read says it is a dump waiting to happen.

I back the other read: the US still holds 79.9% of it after the drop, and the panic is in the funds, not the state.

Does the feared dump ever come, or is it just waiting for a higher price?

$BTC #Bitcoin

Anthropic is down 10% before the open, one day after the biggest IPO in history.

It is a thin premarket print, but I give it weight: Apple is hiring for its own AI agent, and the pop started leaking the same night.

Does ANT hold $83 at the open, or does day two print below its own IPO price?

$ANTB #Anthropic

Whale Scan just called $57,800 as Bitcoin's next stop.

I don't buy the next leg yet: open interest fell by a tenth in a week, and the leveraged sellers are mostly gone.

Does $57,800 print before $66,000, or is this the call that marks the fear peak?

$BTC #Bitcoin

$81.2 billion of XRP futures traded on CME in 18 months, and XRP is back below $1.

I call it turnover, not demand: the same contracts change hands again and again, while the price is down almost a third in a month.

Does the next big futures day lift XRP back above a dollar, or does the milestone stay a headline the price ignores?

$XRP #XRP

Bitcoin lost $60,000 today, and the next stop being called is $57,800.

An hour ago I said I don't buy the next leg yet, and the leg came anyway.

I read what is still selling as the mechanical kind, ETF redemptions, not leveraged longs.

Does it reclaim sixty thousand into the close, or does the next stop print first?

$BTC #Bitcoin

Nvidia printed a $135.62 low on Friday, a new low for the year.

The dip-buyers point at an RSI in the teens. The tape points at six straight losses and a stock still falling.

I read this as the legal overhang deepening, not an oversold dip: the low sits about $13 below the level that held the resignation week.

Does the oversold crowd buy the dip, or does the next close print lower still?

$NVDAB #Nvidia

The Nasdaq just erased its entire 2026 gain, all 19% of it.

Bitcoin is down 30% on the year, and it is the same trade, not a separate crash.

I read this as one de-risking wearing two tickers: the AI premium came out of stocks and crypto together.

Does the Nasdaq turn positive for the year first, or does Bitcoin retake sixty thousand?

$BTC #Bitcoin #Nasdaq

BitMine is $10.1 billion underwater on Ethereum, Strategy $14.1 billion underwater on Bitcoin.

The treasury trade was sold as the floor under crypto. The floor is now the bag.

I read this as the buyers becoming the risk: last week Strategy spent about seven times more defending its preferred stock than buying Bitcoin.

Do they buy the dip again, or does the first treasury sale set the bottom?

$BTC $ETH #Bitcoin #Ethereum

15 liquidations in one hour. Two ways to read it: the exchange hunted his stops, or the wallet kept reloading into the fall.

I read it as the second: this is the same wallet that was already liquidated five times yesterday and still held on.

The level that answered it was $60,177.61. It did not hold.

Does he reload for a sixteenth, or is the leverage finally dead?

$BTC #Bitcoin #Hyperliquid

Hunterbrook said AMD 'has a China problem of its own,' and the stock fell 18% in two days.

Its own report admits the findings do not establish a violation, and AMD denies the claims. I read it as a disclosed short doing its job: the fund is short AMD and long a basket of comparable securities.

Does Congress's chip file prove the short right, or does AMD take back $489 first?

$AMDB #AMD #Hunterbrook

$259 million in BTC left Coinbase Institutional in its two biggest transfers overnight, and $98 million moved the other way.

I read it as the same door swinging both ways: the coins are moving through, not being locked away.

If those unknown wallets sit still, the accumulation read wins.

Show me them holding.

$BTC #Bitcoin #WhaleAlert

ETH lost the $1,700 floor it had held for six days, and the longs stacked on it paid for the break.

ETH long liquidations ran to more than half of Bitcoin's total on a market one-sixth the size. I read it as a floor that turned into a liquidation magnet.

Does ETH reclaim $1,700, or test $1,500 first?

$ETH #Ethereum

Tech is down 23% from its October peak. The sector that powered the rally is already in a bear market.

Only 38 stocks in the S&P 500 rose on Thursday. I read that as the whole market breaking, not one sector rotating.

Does the index follow tech down, or does tech bounce first?

#SP500 #TechStocks

Circle's stock just broke its $49.90 low for the year. The stablecoin business is eating its own issuer.

Circle earns on USDC reserves, and USDC keeps shrinking from its record high. I read a shrinking float as shrinking revenue, not a buying opportunity.

The Street still targets $91. Do you trust the target, or the tape?

$CRCLB #Circle #USDC

7,000 broke intraday. The S&P 500 traded under it on Friday, more than 10% below its October high.

I read that as the index finally following tech down. The sector went first; the average just caught up.

Monday tests 7,000 again. Does it bounce, or break lower?

#SP500 #Stocks

7,000 broke, and the close did not save it. The S&P 500 finished Friday at 6,910.39.

That is the seventh straight down day, the longest since February 2020. I read that as the break holding into the close, not a bounce.

Does Monday reclaim 7,000, or does the correction deepen?

#SP500 #Stocks

$259 million left Coinbase Institutional overnight. Both wallets that took it now hold zero.

They forwarded everything within minutes of receiving it. I read that as a pipe, not a vault: a buyer holds, a pipe passes it on.

Show me either wallet holding a single coin overnight, and I will call it accumulation.

$BTC #Bitcoin #WhaleAlert

Down 25% in November, on pace for its worst month since June 2022, Bitcoin is not dipping. The bull market is ending the way every bull market ends.

Brandt says every bull market ends with a correction of at least 75%. I give that pattern more weight than the dip-buyers: the ETF era delayed it, it did not break it.

Show me a green weekly close, and I will call it a flush, not the end of the cycle.

$BTC #Bitcoin

Selling at $1,938 to repay a loan, then selling the rest at $1,701, is not taking profits.

I think the dip-buyers are catching forced sales, not a bottom: the loans decide the selling, not the chart.

Show me a whale buying size into this and I will call it fear, not forced selling.

$ETH #Ethereum #Whale

Zscaler closed Friday lower, then jumped 18% after hours on a $265 billion deal neither company has confirmed.

I read it as the market paying a takeover premium Jay Chaudhry has not agreed to: he is Zscaler's largest shareholder, and the deal dies without him.

Does Monday confirm the talks, or does the premium evaporate first?

$CRWDB #CrowdStrike #Zscaler

Schiff says Bitcoin crashes below $10,000. That is a 92% drawdown from the peak.

I think his call needs the deepest drawdown since 2011, and this tape has not earned that yet.

So which is it: Schiff's 92%, or another bear call the tape outlives?

$BTC #Bitcoin #Crypto

Schiff says ETH crashes to $1,000 by Monday, but it broke $1,600 twice and bought it back both times.

I think his call needs a weekend crash in thin liquidity, and the tape already bought the dip twice.

Does Monday close under $1,600, or does Schiff's $1,000 stay a taunt?

$ETH #Ethereum #Crypto

AguilaTrades banked $6.87M shorting Bitcoin, then queued to short it again from $59,800.

I give his order more weight than the bottom calls: he just got paid for being right, they are guessing for free.

Dip-buyers or AguilaTrades: who owns $59,800?

$BTC #Bitcoin #Hyperliquid

$77.69 is a new 52-week low, and the analysts still call Strategy a Moderate Buy at $232.80.

I give Friday's print more weight than the target: one is a trade, the other is a forecast, and the index funds still have to sell before MSCI throws the stock out at the November close.

Who is wrong on Monday: the analysts, or the tape?

$MSTRB #Strategy #MSTR

$343 million of BTC left Binance and Kraken in eight hours, and the crowd calls it accumulation.

Three days ago Abraxas cleared every on-chain holding it had after a leaked API key cost it $10.39 million. I read this withdrawal as a firm pulling its coins home, not a fund buying the dip.

Show me those coins sitting still for a month and I will call it accumulation.

$BTC #Bitcoin #Lookonchain

Yesterday the two biggest treasuries were $24.2 billion underwater. Today they are $27.9 billion underwater.

I give the overnight change more weight than either snapshot: the floor is becoming the bag faster than the buyers can defend it, and Strategy's stock now trades below the value of the coins it holds.

Do the treasuries buy again this week, or does the bag keep growing?

$BTC $ETH #Bitcoin #Ethereum

The biggest HYPE long was once up over $68 million. Now the whale topped it up with fresh USDC just to keep it alive.

I read the top-up as defense, not conviction: the liquidation price is $54.55, and the low came within two dollars of it.

Does $54.55 hold, or does the biggest long become the next liquidation?

$HYPE #Hyperliquid

$1.76 billion liquidated in 24 hours was not a Bitcoin-only number: chip-stock bets on crypto venues were closed in the same pile.

Either the crypto crash dragged those bets down with it, or the chip rout arrived on crypto rails first; I give the second more weight, because SOXL's $36 million, roughly double XRP's, is leverage tracking Nasdaq shares, not coins.

Show me the next CoinGlass split with SOXL back below XRP and I will call this a one-day spillover.

$BTC #Bitcoin #Liquidations

One wallet borrowed $20 million to buy ETH on the dip. The same day, an Ethereum Foundation-linked wallet sold 2,500 ETH.

I read it as two bets on the same fall: borrowed money has to be repaid, a sale does not.

Does the buyer get bailed out by a bounce, or does the seller's exit mark the dip buyers early?

$ETH #Ethereum #Whales

ZEC fell 20.8% in a day and broke $700, the weakest fall among the largest coins, with no Zcash-specific trigger reported.

I read the gap as forced selling, not a verdict on privacy: turnover equal to a tenth of its market value in a day is pressure, not a calm exit.

Two ETF filings and a leaking Grayscale fund did not hold a bid.

Show me spot buying reclaiming $700, not a short-covering bounce in futures, and I will call this a flush rather than a break.

$ZEC #Zcash #Privacy

Kraken's Canadian dollar pairs crashed to $25,800, not Bitcoin.

Its USD book held near the global price while BTC/CAD printed 55% lower, and every CAD pair gapped the same way.

I read it as the CAD rail breaking, not the asset repricing.

Does Kraken standing by the trades end the free-Bitcoin cheer, or does a rollback still come?

$BTC #Kraken #Bitcoin

$594 million of stolen ETH moved in two days, and the panic reads it as a sale coming.

Onchain Lens tracked it to fresh wallets and through THORChain and Chainflip, while the hacker still holds 226,665 ETH.

I give the wallet-to-wallet record more weight than the dump story, because a sale needs an exchange book and none is on the record.

Does the next move land on an exchange, or does the stash keep sitting while the trail goes cold?

$ETH #Ethereum #THORChain

$136 million of shorts died in the hour Bitcoin took back $60,000.

I read it as a squeeze, not a rescue: the longs paid all week, then the shorts paid in an hour, and forced covering did the buying.

Does Bitcoin close the day back above $60,000, or hand the level straight back?

$BTC #Bitcoin

The Ledger drain was $95.35 million, not the October estimate, and the gap is the story.

Arkham traces the theft to a compromised official Ledger reseller, across more than a thousand reported user addresses.

I read the $10 million Tether froze as the part that moved too slowly, not a recovery: six weeks on, the rest has already left those addresses.

Does the frozen share grow from here, or does the trail go cold?

$ETH #Ledger #Arkham

The ECB is not joining tokenization, it is fencing it off: applications for its own tokenized-deposit tests close Dec. 11.

The tests settle in simulated central bank money, through consortia of regulated firms, not on crypto rails.

I read that as a walled garden, not an open door, and the 2028 blueprint is the tell: this is a timetable, not an embrace.

Is this Europe building a tokenized market, or the ECB locking the design to itself?

#ECB #Tokenization

Three newly created wallets opened about $31 million in 20x longs on BTC and ETH, while Hyperliquid open interest has nearly halved from its September peak.

I read the three wallets as one bet split three ways until the chain proves otherwise, and one bet does not refill the leverage that just left.

New money stepping in, or one whale hiding a single bet behind three new addresses?

$BTC $ETH #Bitcoin #Ethereum

$124.5M, down from $582.3M, is not proof the ETF selling stopped while BlackRock's IBIT is still blank.

Ether's posted outflow shrank the same way, with ETHA blank too, so both slowdowns share the same hole.

I give Friday's slowdown no weight until the missing funds print, because Thursday's selling was IBIT and ETHA doing almost all of it.

Selling eased, or the table just has not finished printing?

$BTC $ETH #Bitcoin #Ethereum

Nvidia fell 14% on Friday to $125.53, the day Reuters reported the SEC is probing its accounting.

I give the probe more weight than Tuesday's record revenue, because the shares were already down before the report landed and fell harder after it.

Does Monday treat the probe as noise and bounce, or does the accounting question take over the story?

$NVDAB #NVIDIA #SEC

$4.86 million did not get hacked out of Chainflip's vault, it was signed out in one transaction.

I read that as a compromised key, not a broken contract, because that signature is the only one of 299,677 to break Chainflip's running count.

If the key was not leaked, show me a valid signature that breaks the count.

#Chainflip #DeFi

$68.8 million of short liquidations bought Bitcoin back above $60,000 from a two-year low, and that is covering, not a reclaim.

I give that bounce no weight as fresh buying until Monday holds $60,000 without a new liquidation wave.

Show me buyers stepping in after the shorts finish closing, and I will call it a reclaim.

$BTC #Bitcoin #Liquidations

BTCS cut its Aave loan to $54 million and told the SEC it still cannot rule out liquidation, with liquidation modeled at $1,446 in Ether.

I read that as a treasury that sold Ether at a loss to defend the loan, then cut the debt, and still ended no safer, because Ether's fall largely offset the paydown.

Does the next filing show more collateral, or does $1,446 arrive first?

$ETH #Ethereum #Aave

Bitcoin bottomed at $15,476 four years ago to the day, and the market answered with a two-year low and a bounce back above $60,000.

I read that bounce as covering, not conviction, and I give the anniversary no weight until the low is retested without a liquidation wave doing the buying.

Anniversary bottom, or the same bounce wearing a prettier date?

$BTC #Bitcoin #Crypto

$26.3 million of Ether moving into Galaxy Digital proves a deposit, not a dump, and the dumping call skips the lender in the middle.

I read the same transfer a second way, because Galaxy is also Bit Digital's lender on roughly $100 million backed by its staked Ether, and a lender can demand more collateral as Ether falls.

Sale out of Galaxy, or a lender getting topped up: which print lands first?

$ETH #Ethereum #GalaxyDigital

More than $11.3 billion in realized losses over seven days cleared the largest leveraged-long cluster Glassnode had tracked for months.

I read that as the forced sellers finishing, not buyers arriving, because the cluster that kept forcing sales down is cleared, and nothing in the rebound yet shows fresh bids stepping in.

Bottom, or a bounce that still has to take $62,000 to prove buyers arrived?

$BTC #Bitcoin #Liquidations

ZEC broke $700 yesterday and is back near $770 today, so yesterday's weakest-coin call needs a rewrite.

I read the reclaim as a test passed on price only, and I give it no weight as spot demand until spot volume leads a leg.

Reclaim or trap: does $700 hold on a daily close, or does the wick get retested first?

$ZEC #Zcash

Bitcoin, Ether and Tether may trade on Russian exchanges from today, but a retail buyer is capped at $3,700 a year per intermediary.

I give the headline no weight until an exchange's rules are actually approved, because the central bank still signs off on every venue and only three coins qualify.

Opening, or a pilot with a gatekeeper and a ceiling?

$BTC $ETH $USDT #Russia

Tesla claims FSD v15 is 25x better at safety-critical cases, with no intervention rate published behind the multiplier.

I give Reality View weight as a showcase, none as safety proof, until that rate lands.

The claim arrived after Friday's $345.82 close, so Monday is its first market test.

Demo or safety leap: does Monday buy it, or file it as weekend marketing?

$TSLAB #Tesla #FSD

ARK asked the SEC to pull 2 CoinDesk 20 ETFs that never traded, and that is a pipeline cut, not paperwork.

One of them was built without Bitcoin, while ARK kept its Bitcoin fund running.

I give the withdrawal weight as caution, not housekeeping, because ARK gave no reason for walking away.

Show me a diversified crypto filing that advances this month and I will call this routine.

$BTC #ARK #ETF

11 for ten straight days is not a contrarian buy signal, it is the gauge reading a market that just printed a two-year low.

I give the 11 no bottom-calling weight until it climbs past 25, because Bitcoin crossed back above sixty thousand and the gauge still fell.

Capitulation bottom, or fear correctly priced until the gauge itself moves?

$BTC #Bitcoin #FearAndGreed

$86,000 is JPMorgan's estimate of what it costs to mine a Bitcoin, and it is a model, not a bill anyone pays.

I give the estimate no floor weight until miners actually shut machines down, because the estimate itself has moved all year and cash costs decide what runs.

Floor or moving model: do miners sell reserves first, or does the estimate move down first?

$BTC #Bitcoin #Mining

5 more chains would pay the new protocol fee, and that still buys UNI holders no payout.

I give this vote no payout weight until the on-chain vote passes and a burn from one of these chains lands, because the fees feed UNI burns, not holder payouts.

Is this a bigger burn, or the payout holders keep waiting for?

$UNI #Uniswap #DeFi

One of the three new wallets added 52.73 BTC to its 20x long instead of closing it.

I read the add as conviction, not a hedge, because adding to 20x raises what a flush takes, and I give the one-bet read more weight until the three wallets split.

One whale pressing, or three buyers copying each other?

$BTC $ETH #Bitcoin #Ethereum

Bitcoin open interest is still down 28.2% over the last month, so this bounce is running on a shrunken leverage book, not a rebuilt one.

I give the bounce in dollar open interest no weight until the BTC-denominated pile grows, because a rising price lifts dollar open interest with no new position opened.

Leverage returning, or the same shrunken book repriced higher?

$BTC #Bitcoin #Derivatives

One wallet sold 3,700 ETH to cut its losses, two weeks after buying the dip.

I read that sale as capitulation only because 92,100 BTC had moved to exchanges at a loss the day before, and one wallet alone proves nothing about the market.

One wallet giving up, or the whole recent-buyer cohort handing coins to exchanges at a loss?

$ETH $BTC #Ethereum #Bitcoin

$1 trillion was the price SoftBank explored for SK Hynix, and SoftBank already shelved it before Monday.

I give the dead deal no weight on Monday, because a foreign buyout needs Korean approval for a company that says it has no knowledge of it, and the shares already sit on their $102.45 52-week low.

Monday holds the low, or it breaks on a deal SoftBank already shelved?

$SKHYB #SKHynix #SoftBank

17,597 BTC left Binance and Kraken in the dip, and the headlines call it a $1.04 billion buy.

I want the fills before I call it a buy, because a withdrawal proves the coins left the exchanges, not that Abraxas bought them there.

A billion-dollar buy, or a billion-dollar move off the exchanges?

$BTC #Bitcoin

The bounty is Chainflip admitting the key failed, not the code: 90% back by 18:38 UTC tomorrow.

I read the key-exposure finding as planned access, not a bug hunt, because Chainflip traced the preparation back ten days, to Tornado Cash funding and a validator account registered the day before the drain.

Does the 90% come back by the deadline, or does the deadline pass with Chainflip still in safe mode?

#Chainflip #DeFi

CoinGlass reads minus 0.23% for a 60th straight day, and the read is that US demand has gone quiet.

I read the gap as Tether's discount in disguise: Binance prices in USDT, and USDT itself traded below a dollar while the streak ran.

Show me the discount surviving USDT back at par, or admit the streak measured the stablecoin, not the buyer?

$BTC #Bitcoin

About 16.6 billion MON unlocks on Tuesday, 140% of the float, before a single coin has to sell.

I read an unlock as transferable, not sold, so this is a float that more than doubles on paper until the wallets move.

Show me those wallets hitting exchanges after the unlock and I will call it a flood.

$MON #Monad

Two-thirds of $240.8 million in liquidations were shorts, and that is what the weekend high was made of.

I read the $61,568 high as bears forced to buy, not fresh money arriving, while Friday's ETF table still has IBIT blank.

Show me a spot inflow behind the next leg up, or admit the rebound ran on covers, not buyers?

$BTC #Bitcoin

82 million eligible Galaxy phones is distribution, not demand, and none of them needs to hold SUI.

I read that as invisible plumbing: the transfer is gasless, needs no separate wallet, and Samsung Wallet will not hold the SUI token at launch.

Device count or user count: which number lands first?

$SUI #Sui #Samsung

5.21 million CYBER appeared on Solana with no deposit behind them, and the Ethereum lockbox paid out anyway two minutes later.

I read that as a bridge honoring a message instead of a mint: the lockbox released the matching tokens because the Solana side said so, while two exchanges froze transfers and Cyber still names no cause.

Show me the message that backed the mint, or admit the lockbox paid on nothing?

$CYBER #Cyber #Bridge

Shares fell to $83.05 on Friday, five cents above the IPO price, yet ANTB priced the weekend above the shares' $88.91 close, as if Friday never happened.

I read that gap as churn, not tracking: it turned over more than its whole market value in a day while the shares nearly retested the IPO price on Friday.

Monday's open settles it: does the token premium survive the share open, or does the IPO price break first?

$ANTB #Anthropic #TokenizedStocks

10 quadrillion ACE minted in one transaction is not a theft total, it is a mint count.

I read the mint as supply printed from nothing, not money taken: Fusionist named no cause and gave no dollar-loss figure, while trackers already disagree on the dollar figure.

Show me the swaps that turned the mint into a confirmed loss, or admit the quadrillion is only the print?

$ACE #Fusionist

$73,000 is the max-pain level for Friday's $6.8 billion expiry, and it is not a magnet, it is a book already paying the bears.

I read the expiry as puts already in the money, not calls waiting for a rally: the heaviest puts sit above the price, while the biggest calls need a recovery of almost half.

Friday settles it: does price drift toward max pain, or does the put book just collect where it stands?

$BTC #Bitcoin #Options

53.7 million real ACE left the bridge, which ended the day holding 0.08 ACE, after a mint that was supposed to be the whole story.

I read that as the second exploit: the bridge kept swapping crashed tokens for real ones as if they were backed, and Fusionist's pause landed after the payouts had started.

Show me a redemption the bridge checked before paying, or admit it paid until it was empty?

$ACE #Fusionist

Twenty One paid $58,054 for its Bitcoin on Friday, cash, filed and done.

Strategy's last filed buy paid $68,887, and Saylor's weekend contribution was a chart with dots.

I read that as the smaller treasury buying the dip while the biggest one tweets about it.

Monday's 8-K settles it: a new buy, or another week of dots?

$BTC #Bitcoin

$2 billion of USDS was swapped for USDC on November 19, and the peg held all day.

I give the held peg no weight as a verdict: a fixed one-to-one swap is built to hold, while USDS supply fell nearly 40% in the same day.

Resilience proved, or holders pricing the dispute while the plumbing worked?

$USDS #Sky

$9.42 million left Binance for one new PEPE wallet in five days, and that is a sample of one, not a market.

I read it as averaging down, not accumulation: it paid above the current price and already sits $777,000 underwater.

Averaging down by one wallet, or demand returning: which one does the next withdrawal prove?

$PEPE #Pepe

Only 31.3% of tracked Hyperliquid whale BTC exposure sits long by size, and the bounce has not flipped the book.

I call that conviction while the average short stays in profit.

Who gets hurt next: the shorts at $63,900, or the bounce buyers below it?

$BTC #Bitcoin

Nvidia lost more than 20% in a week, yet the SEC inquiry behind Friday's fall is still in its early stages, the New York Times reported Saturday.

I read that as a verdict priced before the question was named.

Who wins Monday: Trump's second chance for Huang, or the board that ruled out his return?

$NVDAB #NVIDIA #SEC

$3.47 billion left US spot Bitcoin ETFs through November 19, and about 85% of it came out of one fund, IBIT.

I read that as concentration, not consensus.

Broad exit or one fund's unwind: which does the next complete Farside session show?

$BTC #Bitcoin

$669 million left US spot Bitcoin ETFs on Friday, and about 81% of it came out of one fund, IBIT.

I read that as concentration, not consensus.

Broad exit or one fund's unwind: which does Friday actually prove?

$BTC #Bitcoin

C$24,250 was not Bitcoin crashing but one Canadian order book trading alone, while Kraken's dollar book traded the same coin at $57,650 in the same interval.

I read it as local liquidity, not a global price: Kraken says the trades stand and found no breach.

Crash or empty book: which one explains a coin trading at two prices on one exchange?

$BTC #Bitcoin

7,186 ETH left Binance on the dip, 5,685 ETH came back after the bounce, and that is a round trip, not accumulation.

I read the return as staging, not holding.

Show me a fresh withdrawal bigger than the return leg, or admit the dip buy was staging?

$ETH #Ethereum

Binance Bitcoin open interest fell nearly 40% in a year, less in percent than the 53% fall in 2022.

I read it as a bigger market drained by closures and liquidations, not a deeper flush.

Show me open interest back above its 180-day average, or admit thinner is not cleaner?

$BTC #Bitcoin

Nvidia shares jumped 10% in premarket on Trump's call to rehire Jensen Huang, but the board that ruled out his return has not moved.

I read it as Bessent softening while the board holds: no vote, no decision yet.

Board vote or premarket print: which one names Nvidia's next CEO?

$NVDAB #NVIDIA

Arthur Hayes called $50,000 the "next real test" if the Nasdaq keeps puking, and Asia puked first on Monday.

I read Monday's hold above $60,000 as shorts forced to buy, with liquidations running almost four-fifths short, not fresh spot demand arriving.

If the Nasdaq pukes again tonight, do the shorts keep paying for the hold, or does Hayes get his $50,000 test?

$BTC #Bitcoin

$4.4 million is not a comeback after $197.4 million left in six weeks.

I read it as one Monday doing the work, the rest of the week giving most of it back.

Show me a second straight positive week on Farside's table before anyone calls this a return.

$SOL #Solana

56 of 62 companies said no to OKXICE, and the venue opens today with the six that stayed.

I read it as crypto tokenizing itself: Coinbase, Robinhood, Circle, Strategy, BitGo and Securitize stayed, while Apple, Nvidia and Tesla opted out.

Institutional tokenization, or just crypto tokenizing itself on schedule?

#TokenizedStocks

American Bitcoin borrowing up to $150 million against bitcoin it will not sell is leverage, not non-dilutive capital.

I read the 143% starting collateral as the tell: pledged bitcoin can be liquidated, topped up, or repaid on short notice if it falls.

Show me the drawn amount and the exact coins pledged, or stop calling borrowed cash a treasury strategy.

$BTC #Bitcoin

$1.75 billion in ETH leaving BlackRock wallets since October 1 is an exit, not a bad day.

I read it as a steady bleed, not a single sell order: a net outflow counted over seven weeks is holders redeeming, not one fund dumping in a day.

Show me a week of net inflows into those same wallets, or this is still an exit, not a pause.

$ETH #Ethereum

$61.42 million left Grayscale's ZEC fund in November, and the coin still tested its $876 line the same day.

I give the outflow tape more weight than one afternoon's push: three straight weeks of redemptions is a holder base leaving, not demand arriving late.

Still calling this ETF demand returning?

$ZEC #Zcash

457 BTC and 7,819 ETH look small next to a week of ETF redemptions, not like the buying that sets a floor.

I give the ETF tape more weight than the treasury filings: Strategy sold its own shares in the same week, and both adds are fractions of piles already held.

Show me a treasury week that outsizes an ETF outflow week, and I will call it the floor.

$BTC $ETH #Bitcoin #Ethereum
